statements.text: My apartment in Tennoji is tiny, and the station is roughly a ten-minute walk away.
Three night shifts a week, working as a nurse on Naniwa General's pediatric ward.
Mochi, my cat, is a rescue who's three years old, and the vacuum cleaner is his absolute enemy.
Every morning I ride the Midosuji line to work, and it's crammed like a sardine can.
Mio, my sister, is a baker at a small boulangerie in Kobe, and she keeps sending me melon pan.
Korean on Duolingo is my new thing, fifteen minutes each day, and it's purely down to K-dramas.
My iPhone 12 is still hanging in there, barely, with the battery gone by lunchtime.
Right now my train playlist is pretty much just Hikaru Utada.
For my birthday Kenta surprised me with a Pixel 9, so the battery panic is over!
I signed up for a yoga class on Saturday mornings near Shinsaibashi.
Since the new year I've been vegetarian, and Osaka makes it easier than I'd expected.
This week I got transferred to the ICU at Naniwa General, and my feet are wrecked.
Mochi now has a little brother in the form of a tabby kitten named Kinako.
I've discovered I'm allergic to shellfish, and I learned it the hard way eating a bowl of ramen in Hakata.
Kenta is an engineer at Panasonic, which means he has a strange no-overtime Wednesday weekly.
Kenta and I have signed on a 2LDK in Fukushima ward and will move in this weekend.
Now I cycle to the hospital, which takes fifteen minutes door to door, and I no longer dread mornings.
Mio has left the boulangerie and is now working for a specialty coffee roaster in Kyoto.
Every Sunday I run along the Yodogawa riverside path, aiming to be ready for a 10k this November.
I traded Duolingo in for a weekly Korean class in Umeda, because I need a real person correcting me.
Kenta's mum is allergic to cats, which is why she arrives with antihistamines whenever she visits.
I dropped the Pixel in the bath and it died, so for now I'm using a spare Galaxy A55 from Kenta.
I'm eating fish again, since being vegetarian didn't survive night shifts, so I'm basically pescatarian now.
I also took up Spanish on Tandem, where I chat with a guy from Valencia on Thursdays.
Signed up for the Himeji Castle 10k on November 8th.
Fujii Kaze now dominates my playlists, with Utada benched.
Today Mochi got his teeth cleaned at the vet, and he sulked for hours afterward.

statements.text: I teach physics and maths at Tertnes high school, and it's my 26th year in the classroom.
The 2014 Volvo V70 diesel is still my car, with 240,000 km on the clock and no sign of dying.
For my blood pressure my doctor prescribed amlodipine, 5 mg each morning.
Odin, our Labrador, has turned nine and is slower when we hit the hills.
Ingrid is a nurse at Haukeland and does mostly day shifts at the moment.
I drink four cups of black filter coffee a day, I know, I know.
There's a clinker dinghy I'm building in the garage, and I've worked on it every Sunday since spring.
Our house sits in Fana, some twenty-five minutes south of the city centre.
Ribbe and aquavit for Christmas Eve, same as every year, and I'm out cold on the sofa by eight.
Most days I get to school on the Bybanen light rail, which gives me time to mark papers.
I've started Italian on Babbel; I'd like to be semi-conversational by the time we go on our trip to Puglia.
The doctor told me to cut the coffee, so now I have two cups a day and green tea in the afternoon.
On the hike up Ulriken my knee gave out, and the MRI says it's a torn meniscus.
Sofie is pregnant, with the baby due in July!
Kari Sunde is our principal, and she'd like me to coach the physics olympiad team.
By the way, Odin is a yellow Lab, and his muzzle is very grey these days.
The arthroscopy on my knee has finally happened, and I'm spending two weeks on crutches, bored out of my mind.
Mats has landed a job as an engineer at Equinor in Stavanger.
On Friday the Model Y arrived and the V70 is gone; I keep reaching for a clutch that doesn't exist.
I also began restoring the rocking chair that belonged to Ingrid's grandfather, and the sanding is a nightmare.
I swapped amlodipine for ramipril because the swollen ankles were a pain.
Friday was the last day before summer break, and I'm off until mid-August.
On Monday Sofie had a baby girl called Linnea, seven pounds something.
This morning I launched the dinghy at Os, christened her Snorre, and she floats!
I've got myself an e-bike and have started cycling to work, forty minutes each way.
Kari Sunde has retired, and our new principal Terje Moe started this week.
Ingrid began French lessons, held on Wednesday evenings, and she's keen.
After the blood pressure scare I've cut coffee out entirely, and it's decaf and herbal tea only.

statements.text: This adobe house on Candelaria has been my home since 1989, and I'm staying put.
Don't bother trying to sell me a smartphone, because my flip phone does everything I need.
I leave the radio on for Pepito the parakeet, who chirps all day long.
For my sugar I take metformin twice a day, and the pharmacist arranged a small weekly pill box for me.
My doctor is Dr. Patel at Lovelace, and he's been looking after me for eleven years.
I'm an alto in the St. Charles choir, and we rehearse Wednesday nights.
Lucia, my daughter in Phoenix, works as a dental hygienist and lectures me about flossing.
For Christmas, Marcus's two kids Mateo and Camila are driving down from Denver to stay.
My 2009 Buick Lucerne is still my ride, with just 61,000 miles on it.
Every morning it's a cafe con leche with two sugars, and no judging.
My left eye's cataract surgery is scheduled for February 3rd.
I joined a bridge club, which meets on Thursday afternoons at the community center.
My cataract surgery went wonderfully, and my left eye can see the blue of the Sandias again.
A neighbor was unable to keep her blue budgie Chula, and now the bird is mine.
Last month Dr. Patel retired, which means I now see Dr. Okafor at the UNM clinic.
Lucia persuaded me to get an iPhone SE, and I'm learning to FaceTime the grandkids.
The garden is back in business, with tomatoes and green chile in the ground.
Elena, my daughter-in-law, is a pharmacist at Kaiser, and every Sunday she sends me photos.
Because my A1C was too high, Dr. Okafor added Jardiance to the metformin, one pill every morning.
I sold the Candelaria house and relocated to a one-bedroom at Sandia Vista on the east side.
The neighbor's grandson bought my Buick, and with the shuttle at Sandia Vista I don't miss driving.
Yesterday I had lunch with Rosa at Garduno's, and the sopapillas were enormous.
Now it's just a pot of basil on the balcony; the tomato days are behind me.
The audiologist set me up with Phonak hearing aids, and I can hear the choir again.
This week Pepito died in his sleep at eleven years old, and I cried more than I'd expected.
I've switched my cafe con leche to decaf because my pressure's been creeping up.
Since Dr. Okafor left the UNM clinic, I'm seeing a nurse practitioner, Brenda Wells, at the Sandia Vista clinic.

statements.text: At Brightwater Builders I work as a structural engineer, mostly on high-rise work around Lekki.
Our three-bedroom flat in Yaba is rented, and the landlord keeps promising to fix the water pump.
I drive a 2011 Toyota Camry, Tokunbo, and the AC is the only part that complains.
It's about ninety minutes each way to get to site, and Third Mainland Bridge is my sworn enemy.
My wife Ngozi works as a pharmacist at a hospital in Ikeja.
The landlord sold the building, so we moved to a flat in Surulere, and boxes are still everywhere.
Every Saturday morning I play five-a-side football; my knees hate me, but the banter's worth it.
Petrol powers the generator in our compound, and the fuel bill is killing me.
Our first baby is due in March, for Ngozi and me!
I use a Tecno Camon 30 as my phone, and honestly its camera is decent.
I spent Christmas in Enugu with my parents; my mum's jollof can't compete with Lagos jollof, but don't tell her.
I'm trying out intermittent fasting: sixteen hours off, with nothing to eat after 7pm.
My PMP exam is booked for 14 May, and I study every night after dinner.
Last week the solar panels and an inverter were installed, and I sold the generator to my cousin.
Chidi was born on the 4th at 3.4 kg and already has Ngozi's frown.
All of Chidi's first-month photos are on my iPhone 14, which is new to me, and the Tecno lives in a drawer now.
I've resigned from Brightwater and on Monday I start as a senior structural engineer at Arcadia Infrastructure.
I do French on Busuu for twenty minutes before bed, just in case Arcadia ever sends me to Abidjan.
PMP passed!! Those four months of misery paid off.
My new office is on Victoria Island, so now I leave at 5:30am and get there in about an hour.
I've dropped the fasting experiment; with a newborn at home, sleep beats an eating window.
At the end of September the Ikoyi tower package is due to the client.
Folake Bankole is my manager at Arcadia, and I love that she keeps meetings short.
Obinna, my younger brother, works as a junior doctor in Manchester.
The deadline for the Ajah estate package is mid-December, so that one can wait.
The Camry has finally gone to the scrapyard, and I got a 2016 Honda CR-V from a dealer in Lekki.
Dr. Adeyemi, a very serious man, is Ngozi's boss at the hospital.
I've just been made principal structural engineer at Arcadia, three months in, and I'm still processing it.

statements.text: Studio is eating my entire life in the final year of my architecture degree at RMIT.
I live in a share terrace in Brunswick East with three housemates, and one of them steals my yoghurt.
I work at a bike shop on Sydney Road at weekends, where it's mostly puncture repairs and bad coffee.
I take the tram to uni, the 96, when it actually turns up.
The screen of my Pixel 7 is a spiderweb, yet it still works, so I haven't upgraded yet.
I've found out I'm lactose intolerant, which accounts for four years of stomach aches, so from now on I'm on oat flat whites.
My 2019 MacBook Pro is still what I use, and its fan sounds like a jet engine.
Vegetarian is what I've been since my birthday in October; mum is coping.
Fine, Spotify, I admit it: I did listen to Phoebe Bridgers for nine hundred minutes last year.
I splurged on a MacBook Air M3 using my bike-shop savings, and the jet engine has retired.
I've started bouldering at Northside on Tuesday nights, and my forearms are not impressed.
I'm learning Japanese on WaniKani, ten minutes each morning before my coffee.
Jonas, my brother, is a FIFO electrician in the Pilbara, working two weeks on and one off.
I signed a lease on my own one-bedroom in Northcote, and finally there's some quiet.
Now I go by bike, thirty minutes along the Merri Creek trail into the city.
Ten days in Kyoto are done, and my Japanese made it through a ramen vending machine.
In case anyone asks, the bike is an olive-green Surly Cross-Check.
I've quit the bike shop and I'm interning three days a week at Fenwick+Lowe, a small studio in Collingwood.
I'm writing my thesis on the adaptive reuse of old Brunswick warehouses.
I'm going vegan for June, and quite possibly for good, and my nan is horrified.
I've signed up for Auslan classes on Thursday nights since sign language has always fascinated me.
The vegan month is finished and I gave in; I'm back to vegetarian since cheese won.
I'm on day three with my new iPhone 15 and I already miss the Pixel's camera.
I deleted Spotify and moved my playlists over to Apple Music, since I'm on the iPhone now.
The warehouses had to go at my supervisor's insistence, so the thesis is now a timber community library.
I've got about eleven pages, and thesis submission is the 30th of October.
It's late nights all round because the Fenwick+Lowe competition entry is due on the 14th of October.

statements.text: This week was my start as a pastry chef at Maison Verdier here in Lyon, and the croissants alone justify the 4am alarm.
I rent a tiny studio in Croix-Rousse, fifth floor, with no elevator, and my calves are filing a complaint.
Biscotte, my tabby, is six and gets deeply offended whenever I'm home on a Sunday.
I bike to work along the Rhône, which takes about 25 minutes if the wind behaves.
I'm trying to learn Spanish with Duolingo, ten minutes in bed each night before I pass out.
A cruel joke for a pastry chef: I'm allergic to hazelnuts. My epi pen is always with me.
My mornings begin with a double espresso from my stovetop moka pot, no sugar and no conversation.
Théo, my boyfriend, works as a sound engineer at a little radio station near Part-Dieu.
I have a Samsung Galaxy S21 for a phone, and its battery dies by lunchtime.
Every Tuesday and Thursday evening I run 5k loops in Parc de la Tête d'Or.
On baking days my go-to album is Mordechai by Khruangbin.
The doctor told me to cut the caffeine, so now I drink genmaicha tea in the mornings.
I adopted a second cat from the shelter, a shy little black one named Madeleine.
I've handed in my notice at Maison Verdier, and next Monday I start at Café Lumière as head of pastry!
Today I unboxed an iPhone 16, and the camera is unreal for food shots.
At last Théo and I have moved into a two-bedroom in Villeurbanne, which has an actual elevator.
According to the vet, Biscotte weighs a chunky seven kilos, so she's on a diet and furious about it.
Because Café Lumière is across town, I take tram T1 now, and I finally get to read on my commute.
My knee has been angry since May, and the doctor has banned running, so it's swimming twice a week at the municipal pool instead.
I also signed up for Italian classes on Tuesday evenings, since why suffer in just one language.
On Friday I had dinner with my sister Inès at that Lebanese place, and she cried over the baklava.
Lately I bake to Lux by Rosalía.
It turns out I'm mildly allergic to kiwi as well; my mouth went itchy at brunch.
Plot twist: coffee is back for me, strictly decaf, made in the old moka pot.
Théo left the radio station and now works as a sound designer at a video game studio in Lyon.

statements.text: The school year starts on Monday. I've been teaching physics and maths at Älvsborgsskolan for 27 years, and somehow I still enjoy it.
Our home is a red villa in Mölndal, just outside Gothenburg, with white corners, naturally.
My car is a 2014 Volvo V70 diesel with 240,000 km on the clock, and I have zero plans to part with it.
Sture, our dog, is a golden retriever aged nine who treats every walk like a polar expedition.
Every morning at 6, rain or shine, Sture gets three kilometres. I bought myself a headlamp for the dark months.
My blood pressure was a bit high at my checkup, so I take 5 mg of amlodipine every morning.
I have a ThinkPad T480 as my laptop, and I refuse to retire it.
I go to a woodworking course on Wednesday evenings, where I'm building a Shaker-style cabinet.
Linnea, my daughter, is a veterinarian up in Uppsala, mostly horses and the occasional angry goat.
Karin's car is a white Toyota Yaris hybrid, and she brags about the fuel economy constantly.
I traded in the old Volvo for a second-hand Nissan Leaf, and it's so quiet that the dog doesn't hear me coming.
My blood pressure is still stubborn, so the doctor has doubled my amlodipine to 10 mg.
The woodworking course ended last night. The cabinet is done and now sits in our hallway.
Pelle, a one-eyed cat, more or less adopted Karin and me, so we took the cat in.
Because Sture's hips are going downhill, mornings are a gentle one kilometre nowadays.
This is being typed on my new MacBook Air, whose battery keeps going and going.
I've left the classroom for good and I'm now a lab instructor at Chalmers' physics department, with no more teenagers hiding phones under desks.
With sailing season open, I race a Laser dinghy with the Mölndal club on Sunday mornings.
Mattias, Karin's boss at the pharmacy, bakes cardamom buns for the whole team every Friday.
My ankles puffed up like balloons, so the doctor replaced the amlodipine with losartan.
I swapped the Leaf for a used Skoda Enyaq because its winter range was a joke.
My Enyaq is the 80 version, in dark green, and the dog crate fits perfectly in the back.
On Friday I went to a tribute concert for Esbjörn Svensson at the Konserthuset, with goosebumps all night.
I'm unpacking boxes in our new place in Linné, and central Gothenburg is a lot louder than Mölndal ever was.
I also joined a men's choir; we rehearse on Tuesday nights and I'm a second tenor.

statements.text: Interface design is my job at a fintech startup called Finlo here in Bangalore, which means my days are Figma and arguments about button radii.
Divya, my manager, is great; she actually reads my design docs.
I share a three-bedroom flat in Indiranagar with two roommates, and the rent is eye-watering.
Every day I ride a scooter to the office, 35 minutes if Old Airport Road behaves.
A OnePlus 9 is my phone, and it's still going strong three years on.
I've been a vegetarian all my life; mom would disown me otherwise.
I play badminton with the Koramangala crew on Saturday mornings, 7am sharp.
I'm learning Kannada since my landlord only speaks Kannada and I'm tired of smiling and nodding.
I plan to apply for the HCI master's at TU Delft, and the deadline is in December.
Arjun, my brother, works at Infosys in Pune, doing backend stuff he refuses to explain.
I bought my scooter, a matte grey Honda Activa, second-hand from a colleague.
Everyone on the team is sleeping under their desks because Project Lotus ships on 15 December.
Project Atlas, my other assignment, isn't due until the end of January.
There's been a reorg at work: Karthik is my manager now, and Divya has moved over to the payments team.
Notion holds all my work notes, using a color-coded system that nobody else understands.
Sneha, my roommate, is a corporate lawyer, and she bills more per hour than I earn per day.
My iPhone 15's camera makes my food photos look way better than they deserve.
My iron was low at my checkup, so I'm not strictly vegetarian any more; eggs are in.
I've decided to skip the Delft master's, and the money goes toward a flat down payment instead.
My last day at Finlo was last Friday, and tomorrow I start at Orchard Health as a senior product designer.
Meera, my manager at Orchard, is ex-Google and asks scary good questions.
I take the metro now because Orchard's office is right by the Purple Line, and the scooter's just collecting dust in the parking lot.
I moved into my own 1BHK in HSR Layout, my first time living alone, and it's glorious.
I've also taken up French on Duolingo, just for fun.
I switched from badminton to bouldering, on Saturday mornings at a climbing gym in HSR.
I saw Prateek Kuhad live at Palace Grounds on Friday, and my voice is completely gone.
I've started using Obsidian for my personal notes, while Notion stays for work stuff.

statements.text: I work as a freelance photographer, mostly shooting weddings and corporate headshots around São Paulo.
Our rented apartment is in Vila Madalena, on the third floor, and the neighbours' samba nights are free entertainment.
I shoot with a Canon R6 body, about 40k frames through it so far.
I drive a Fiat Argo, which is perfect for squeezing into São Paulo parking spots.
Lucas, who's eight, goes to Colégio Santa Maria and is obsessed with dinosaurs.
Pipoca, our dog, is a three-year-old caramel vira-lata and steals socks.
I've got a Moto G54 for a phone, cheap and cheerful.
Tuesday and Thursday nights are jiu-jitsu, and after two years I'm still a blue belt.
I've been trying low-carb since last month: no rice, no bread, which is brutal in Brazil.
Camila, my wife, is a dentist who has her own clinic in Pinheiros.
Bia has just turned five and goes to a little school called Pequeno Príncipe; every day she comes home covered in paint.
Thiago, my brother, drives a black Jeep Renegade and is convinced it makes him an adventurer.
The Canon is sold, and I got a Sony A7 IV; its autofocus tracking is witchcraft.
Camila has a Pixel 8 for a phone, and she never lets me forget its camera beats mine.
The low-carb phase lasted four months, and I'm back on rice and beans like a normal Brazilian.
I've joined Estúdio Lume as lead photographer, which means no more chasing invoices as a freelancer.
I filmed Lucas's school recital on my new iPhone 15 Pro, and the stabilization is absurd.
I traded the Argo in for a Hyundai HB20 with automatic transmission, and my left leg thanks me.
We've moved to a house in Granja Viana, forty minutes outside the city, and we finally have a garden.
New house means new school: Lucas now goes to Escola Vila Verde and made a best friend named Davi in week one.
Lucas is building a football goal out of PVC pipes in the little yard at the new place.
My shoulder said enough, so I quit jiu-jitsu. My new thing is Wednesday night futsal with the neighbourhood guys.
At a rescue fair we adopted a tiny grey cat, and Bia named her Mel.
Plot twist: I'm shooting everything on a Fujifilm X-T5 and the Sony is gone; the film simulations are addictive.
I also picked up a DJI Mini 4 drone for aerial shots, and wedding clients go nuts for them.
Last Saturday I shot a wedding in Campos do Jordão, eleven hours on my feet.

statements.text: For 31 years, Walt and I have been living in the same two-story house in Westerville, Ohio.
My car is a 2015 Buick Encore, and it's been a faithful little car.
A flip phone is still what I use. I can't see why anyone needs more than that.
I'm scheduled for my knee replacement on December 8th, wish me luck.
Marmalade, my cat, is seventeen and sleeps on my side of the bed.
For my cholesterol, an atorvastatin goes down every night right before bed.
The surgery went fine! For now I'm getting around the house on a walker.
Saturdays are still workdays for Walt at the hardware store; he says retirement is overrated.
I have Phonak hearing aids, and the left one keeps whistling at me.
The book club gets together at the library on the first Thursday of every month.
You'll find me in the hospital gift shop on Monday mornings; after thirty-eight years of nursing I still can't stay away.
No more walker, just a cane now, and the physical therapist says I'm ahead of schedule.
Jenny, my daughter, and her family live in Seattle, and I'm visiting them in June.
We adopted a rescue beagle called Hank, who's three years old and howls at the mailman.
Thanks to Jenny setting me up with an iPhone SE, I'm now texting the grandkids emojis nonstop.
I joined a knitting circle at church too, Fridays at ten.
I traded the Buick in for a Subaru Forester, because higher seats are kinder to the new knee.
Walt thinks it's hilarious that the Forester is forest green.
That 2008 F-150 that Walt refuses to sell is still what he drives.
Because of muscle aches, my doctor swapped the atorvastatin for rosuvastatin.
The cane is in the closet; today I walked the whole neighborhood loop without it!
I got new rechargeable Oticon hearing aids, so no more fumbling with tiny batteries.
We've sold the old house and moved to a one-floor ranch in Hilliard with no stairs at all.
Last night Marmalade died, curled up on my side of the bed. I'm a mess.
Since the library room got double-booked, book club has moved to the second Tuesday evening of the month, at Jan's house.
I've quit the hospital gift shop, and now on Monday mornings I read to kids at the library.
On Saturday I took my grandson Owen to the zoo, and he named every single penguin.
